title: Jude and the Harbor
premise: During the brutal storm season of 1893, widowed lighthouse keeper Orsen Delacroix keeps the light burning on a lonely harbor point while the coastal authorities begin rounding up foreign sailors suspected of espionage. When a frightened boy named Jude is left at her door with a note reading 'forget the face,' Orsen recognizes the handwriting of Tomas Vey, the fisherman who once saved her husband's life and whom she promised any debt repaid. Sheltering Jude makes her a criminal, and as the magistrate closes in and the boy's true parentage implicates a family Orsen thought long dead to her, she must choose between the law that pays her wage and the memory of a promise. In the end, she smuggles Jude out on the last fishing boat before the final storm, testifies to nothing, loses the lighthouse, and gains something she never expected: a family of choice waiting in a free port.
about_author: Ansel Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs from the North Atlantic coast. Their fiction draws on the quiet heroism of keepers, smugglers, and the people history forgot to record.
